lessons.title: Basic Navigation
lessons.content:
# Basic Navigation

The shell (or terminal) is a command-line interface for interacting with your operating system.

### Essential Commands
- `pwd`: Print Working Directory. Shows where you are.
- `ls`: List files and directories in the current folder.
- `cd <dir>`: Change Directory. Move to a different folder.
- `cd ..`: Move up one directory level.
- `cd ~`: Move to your home directory.

```bash
pwd
ls -la # list all files with detailed info
cd Documents
```

lessons.title: File Operations
lessons.content:
# File Operations

Create, move, copy, and delete files and folders from the command line.

### Commands
- `touch <file>`: Create an empty file.
- `mkdir <dir>`: Create a new directory.
- `cp <source> <dest>`: Copy a file or directory (`-r` for recursive).
- `mv <source> <dest>`: Move or rename a file or directory.
- `rm <file>`: Remove (delete) a file.
- `rm -rf <dir>`: Remove a directory and its contents recursively and forcibly (Use with caution!).

lessons.title: File Permissions
lessons.content:
# File Permissions

Every file and directory has permissions for the Owner, Group, and Others.

### Permission Types
- **Read (r)**: value 4
- **Write (w)**: value 2
- **Execute (x)**: value 1

### chmod Command
Used to change permissions.
```bash
chmod 755 script.sh # rwxr-xr-x
chmod +x script.sh  # add execute permission
```
`755` means: Owner has 7 (r+w+x), Group has 5 (r+x), Others have 5 (r+x).

lessons.title: Piping & Redirection
lessons.content:
# Piping & Redirection

### Redirection
- `>`: Redirect output to a file (overwrites).
- `>>`: Append output to a file.
- `<`: Redirect input from a file.

```bash
echo "Hello" > hello.txt
```

### Piping (`|`)
Passes the output of one command as input to another.
```bash
cat file.txt | grep "search_term"
```

lessons.title: Grep, Sed & Awk
lessons.content:
# Grep, Sed & Awk

Powerful tools for searching and manipulating text.

- **grep**: Search for patterns in text.
  `grep "error" log.txt`
- **sed**: Stream editor for filtering and transforming text.
  `sed 's/old/new/g' file.txt` (replace 'old' with 'new')
- **awk**: Pattern scanning and processing language, great for column-based data.
  `ls -l | awk '{print $9, $5}'` (print filename and size)

lessons.title: Viewing File Content
lessons.content:
# Viewing File Content

- `cat`: Display the entire file.
- `less`: View file content one page at a time (interactive).
- `head -n 10`: View the first 10 lines.
- `tail -n 10`: View the last 10 lines.
- `tail -f`: Follow a file in real-time (useful for logs).

lessons.title: Variables & Script Structure
lessons.content:
# Shell Scripting

A shell script is a file containing a series of commands.

### Shebang
The first line tells the system which interpreter to use.
```bash
#!/bin/bash
```

### Variables
```bash
NAME="Alice"
echo "Hello $NAME"
```
Note: No spaces around the `=` sign during assignment.

lessons.title: Control Flow
lessons.content:
# Control Flow in Shell

### If Statements
```bash
if [ "$AGE" -ge 18 ]; then
  echo "Adult"
else
  echo "Minor"
fi
```

### For Loops
```bash
for i in {1..5}; do
  echo "Iteration $i"
done
```

lessons.title: Functions & Arguments
lessons.content:
# Functions & Arguments

### Arguments
- `$0`: Name of the script.
- `$1`, `$2`: First and second arguments.
- `$#`: Number of arguments.
- `$@`: All arguments.

### Functions
```bash
greet() {
  echo "Hello $1"
}
greet "World"
```
